newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Panamax erosion seems halted.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Panamax erosion seems halted.

text.p: The recent slow erosion of Panamax voyage and timecharter rates appears to have been halted.

Former conditions for the TransAtlantic rounds were evident from a number of grains fixtures and there were also signs of steadier levels for Panamaxes in the East. Capers were said to be in fair demand in the Pacific, although the Atlantic market for these types is believed to be less promising, brokers added. The BFI recorded its first gain since November 13, up four points to 1,427. GRAIN The extent of Cargill Panamax chartering activities took brokers by surprise, especially following the American holiday at the end of last week.
Some firm rates were said by market sources to have been conceded for Transatlantic business, although confirmation was lacking from Cargill themselves on both the rates and the loading areas.

Marguesa 70,312 dwt which passed Passero November 24 was believed book by Cargill at $11,500 daily, 1977-built Kosmaj 72,050 dwt prompt W Med at $8,500 daily and the 1974-built Dora Oldendorff 73,974 dwt at $8,000 daily. Kavo Deklfini 64,583 dwt open spot Gibraltar was also linked with Cargill for similar business. Even in the East these charterers were active, fixing the 1982-built Irene Oldendorff 62,210 dwt delivery spot Japan for a trip via Australia to the Egyptian Med at a steady $8,250 daily. Some brokers believe that the supply of Panamax tonnage able to load in the Plate in December is tightening. MINERALS Some leading Caper brokers were forecasting the decline of Caper rates in the Atlantic but there was little immediate news at this early stage of the week to support such a view. Thalassini Axia 164,796 dwt was rumoured fixed in the Pacific on private terms. Panamax tonnage featured in reports that Navix booked Nordmoritz 72,500 dwt in direct continuation from Japan Decemnber 8 for a Pacific round at a solid $12,200 daily.
